artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of the Florence copy of
Lesley's 1755 Mozarabic Missal, 20,253 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR
bytes, no form feeds, no NUL bytes, ending in a newline. Registered as a source
artifact and nothing more; deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records.
THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES IN THIS FILE.

WHY THIS COPY IS HELD AS WELL AS THE NEW YORK ONE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS
ARTIFACT. It is the copy that runs to the end of the book. Its last text leaf,
n591 of 761, prints the explicit -- `Ad laudem omnipotentis Dei, necnon Virginis
Marie matris ejus: omnium Sanctorum Sanctarumque. Expletum est Missale Mixtum
secundum regulam Beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes: maxima cum diligentia perlectum
& emmendatum per Reveren...` -- preceded by the Benedictio panis and the Mass of
the Blessed Virgin. THE NEW YORK COPY THE ACT HISTORY NAMES STOPS AT ITS LEAF
n401, part way through the sanctoral, with no explicit at all. The commissioning
brief for this lane described this item as a duplicate of that one. It is not,
and guidance/sources.md names both halves of the failure that would have
followed: a false absence, where the end of a book is held under a name nobody
searched, and a false duplicate, where two copies drift and nothing compares
them. They are compared here and in the edition record.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS BAD -- WHICH IS THE PRICE OF THE COMPLETENESS. Measured
here by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin function-word share of 0.0509 over
108,392 tokens, English 0.0207, classified `degraded-latin`. That is the lowest
figure in this acquisition, lower even than the 1499 incunable's 0.0537, and far
below the 0.1294 of the New York copy of the same edition. THE TWO ARE THE SAME
TYPESETTING, so the difference is entirely the imaging and the recognition, not
the book: this file emits long stretches of word-shaped rubble
(`rep™ ©■ acciphnt ab eo «rcj inrriijj`) where the New York file emits readable
Latin. DO NOT REST A NEGATIVE SEARCH ON THIS ARTIFACT. Its role is to establish
that the end of the book exists, to bound it, and to be the file a later reader
goes to the page images for. Where the two copies overlap, READ THE NEW YORK ONE
AND USE THIS ONE ONLY BEYOND ITS BREAK. It is admitted `indexable` so that later
passages can pin physical line ranges over it, not so that a search over it can be
reported as a finding.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The title page is at
leaf n7. Monaldini's dedication to Benedict XIV opens at n11. Lesley's long
critical preface, arguing the relation of the Mozarabic liturgy to the Gallican
and to the Bobbio sacramentary, runs from about n28 to about n120. The Missal
itself follows. The Mass of the Blessed Virgin is at n585, the Benedictio panis
at n590, the explicit at n591. Leaves after n591 carry the indexes -- `MENSIS
MARTII. MENSIS JUNII. INDEX RERUM.` -- and Google's end sheets.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `bub_gb_hAJaQabODUYC`, 761 leaves,
`imagecount = 761`, matching the 761 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's own
djvu.xml counted here. Google id hAJaQabODUYC, contributor National Central
Library of Florence, uploaded 2014-08-25 by `tools.bub@tools.wmflabs.org`. Its
Internet Archive title, `... Pars prima secunda`, is the reason the leaf count is
nearly double the New York copy's; a title page for a second part was searched
for and NOT found in the per-leaf recognition, so whether the volume is a single
continuous impression or two parts bound together IS NOT SETTLED HERE and is not
asserted either way. What is settled is where the text stops in each copy, which
is what a reader needs. The companion page-image container is the item's
`bub_gb_hAJaQabODUYC.pdf`, 13,372,022 bytes, which is not registered.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. `read_from =
"not-read"` on the Mozarabic witness rows in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record. Nothing in this repository has read a
unit of the Mozarabic use.
artifacts.rights_basis:
Public domain in the United States because the book was first published outside
the United States before the pre-1931 line, and on that ground alone.

THE LINE, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published abroad before
1931 is out of United States copyright; that is the line guidance/missals.md
records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE
MOVES EVERY JANUARY -- guidance/missals.md:249 states it in terms -- so it is
written here as DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on
1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932, and a later reader must re-derive it
rather than quote this sentence. Publication at Rome in 1755 clears the 2026 line
by a hundred and seventy-six years. URAA restoration cannot reach it: a restored
term runs at most 95 years from publication, which for 1755 ended in 1850.

THE DATE WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN PAGES. The title page at leaf n7 of
761 reads `... AB ALEXANDRO LESLEO S. J. SACERDOTE ORNATUM. PARS PRIMA.
Sumptibus Venantii Monaldini Bibliopolae in Via Cursus. TYPIS JOANNIS GENEROSI
SALOMONI`, and the corresponding leaf of the sister copy carries the imprint year
`ROMAE MDCCLV` on the same setting. A thirty-two-probe anachronism battery over
all 761 leaves found St Pius X absent, the Queenship absent, St Joseph the Worker
absent, Christ the King absent, St Therese absent, the Immaculate Heart absent,
`Signum magnum` and its dropped-initial form `ignum magnum` absent, the 1960
class ranks absent, the Immaculate Conception dogma absent, and no arabic year
later than the imprint on any leaf. The probes and their negatives are listed in
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml. The volume ends
at the work's own explicit on leaf n591, `Expletum est Missale Mixtum secundum
regulam Beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes`, with no supplement and no second
imprint. This test was run because two acquisitions had already been refused for
failing it, the 1920 Missale Romanum and the Braga digitisation.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical
reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art
Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was
produced autonomously by ABBYY FineReader 9.0, per the item's own `ocr` field,
converted by `abbyy-to-hocr 1.1.11`, and there is no author to hold a right in it.
Bridgeman's limit -- it frees a scan of public-domain matter and says nothing
about a scan of anything else -- bites on nothing here: every leaf of this file
is a photograph of a page printed in 1755.

THE GOOGLE QUESTION. The book was scanned by Google for the National Central
Library of Florence. THIS FILE DOES NOT CARRY GOOGLE'S `Usage guidelines` PAGE:
the Wikimedia `bub` upload chain stripped it, and the only Google matter is the
watermark surviving as OCR noise. The sister artifact of this same edition,
`missale-mixtum-1755-nypl-text-ed70e3ae`, does carry it, and the position on it
is stated once in the rights record and applies wherever it appears.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item carries `licenseurl =
http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/`. guidance/sources.md:395-400
holds the first two insufficient for `tracked`, and the third is a fact about an
item's metadata rather than about a book -- the ground refused at
src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml.

artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of the New York Public
Library copy of Lesley's 1755 Mozarabic Missal, 53,824 LF-terminated lines, valid
UTF-8, no CR bytes, no form feeds, no NUL bytes, ending in a newline. Registered
as a source artifact and nothing more; deliberately NOT structured as liturgical
records. THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES IN THIS FILE except the Google front
matter's, which is a boundary in the scanning and not in the book.

THIS COPY IS INCOMPLETE AND THE ACT HISTORY CALLS IT WHOLE. Its last text leaf,
n401 of 408, breaks off inside the sanctoral at `IN JEJUNIO KALENDARUM
NOVEMBRIUM` under a running head `FESTA MENS[IS]`. There is no explicit, no
colophon and no end matter; the remaining leaves are blank and Google's end
sheets. src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml, witness row
1755-missale-mixtum-lesley, describes the station this item digitises as `the
first edition of the rite anyone here can read whole`, and the edition is that;
THIS COPY OF IT IS NOT. The complete text is in the sibling artifact
`missale-mixtum-1755-florence-text-c52ac184`, which runs to the work's explicit
on its leaf n591. The row was not edited -- the act-history inventories were
outside this lane's ownership -- and the correction is recorded at
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS THE BEST OF THE TWO 1755 COPIES BY A LARGE MARGIN.
Measured here by scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin function-word share of 0.1294
over 205,273 tokens, English 0.0321, classified `prose-latin` -- against 0.0509
for the Florence copy of the very same typesetting. The item was scanned at 600
ppi, the highest in this acquisition. The damage that remains is ordinary for a
1755 roman-type folio: long s read as f, the ae-digraph unstable, and the
occasional dropped ornamental initial (`UoD sumptibus meis prodit Missale
Mozarabicum` for Quod). WHERE THE TWO COPIES OVERLAP, READ THIS ONE. Use the
Florence copy only beyond this one's break at n401.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Google's `Usage
guidelines` page occupies lines 1 to about 43 and is not part of the book. The
title page is at leaf n11, lines 47-64. Monaldini's dedication to Benedict XIV is
at n15. Lesley's critical preface runs from about n28 to about n120, with its
footnote apparatus; the note at line 1676 reading `t. Lat. Venetiis 1759` is the
one unresolved date in the file and is discussed in the edition record. The
Missal itself follows from about n130, with the Ordinary and Canon in the middle
of the volume -- the fraction and the rubric `si forte aliqua pars hostie maneat
plicata in filiole corporalium` stand at n295. The text stops at n401.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `missalemixtumse00leslgoog`, 408
leaves, `imagecount = 408`, matching the 408 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's own
djvu.xml counted here. Google id mr8PAAAAIAAJ, OCLC 44008910, OpenLibrary
OL20619112M, contributor New York Public Library, scanned 2006-08-02, uploaded
2009-04-15 by `tpb`, `volume = 1`. The companion page-image container is the
item's `missalemixtumse00leslgoog.pdf`, 28,715,021 bytes, which is not registered.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. `read_from =
"not-read"` on the Mozarabic witness rows in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record.

THE DATE WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN PAGES. The title page at leaf n11 of
408 reads `MISSALE MIXTUM SECUNDUM REGULAM BEATI ISIDORI DICTUM MOZARABES,
PRAEFATIONE, NOTIS, ET APPENDICE AB ALEXANDRO LESLEO S. J. SACERDOTE ORNATUM.

absent, St Joseph the Worker absent, Christ the King absent, St Therese absent,
the Immaculate Heart absent, `Signum magnum` and its dropped-initial form `ignum
magnum` absent, the 1960 class ranks absent, and the Immaculate Conception dogma
absent. Its one hit was `Missale Romanum S. Pii Quinti` in Lesley's preface,
where he argues that the Mozarabic Masses are no less sacred for differing from
the Roman book -- a scholar of 1755 discussing 1570. The probes and their
negatives are listed in
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical

Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it: this text layer was
produced autonomously by ABBYY FineReader 8.0 at 600 ppi, per the item's own
`ocr` field, and there is no author to hold a right in it.

THE ONE PLACE BRIDGEMAN DOES NOT REACH IN THIS FILE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE
BRAGA RECORD'S WHOLE LESSON IS THAT THE EXACT ARTIFACT IS WHAT `tracked` GOVERNS.
Lines 1 to about 43 of this file are not a photograph of a 1755 page. They are
GOOGLE'S OWN `Usage guidelines`, modern prose of Google's authorship, scanned in
at the front of the volume: `Google is proud to partner with libraries to
digitize public domain materials...`, `+ Make non-commercial use of the files We
designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use
these files for personal, non-commercial purposes`, `+ Maintain attribution The
Google "watermark" you see on each file is essential... Please do not remove it`.
Bridgeman says nothing about that text, because it is not a reproduction of
anything; it is new writing of the 2000s. THE POSITION TAKEN HERE, AND IT IS A
POSITION AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT, is that this page may be redistributed with the
file because Google wrote and inserted it precisely to travel with the file and
asks in it that the attribution not be removed -- an implied licence to
redistribute the notice unaltered, which is what is done. The notice's
non-commercial sentence is framed as a REQUEST (`we request that you use`) and
not as a condition of a licence to the book, and Google's own text in the same
breath says `Public domain books belong to the public and we are merely their
custodians`; it asserts no copyright in the 1755 book or in the scan of it. The
whole of the rest of this file is the book. Nothing in this repository quotes the
notice as source text, and if a later reader wants the file without it, deleting
lines 1-43 is a stated replayable transformation on a boundary the file actually
has -- unlike the Braga carve-out, which had no such boundary anywhere.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the item is marked `possible-copyright-status =
NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT`. guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds the first two insufficient
for `tracked`, and the third is a host's guess about a book, recorded as a fact

edition.authority: None. `Superiorum permissu` on the title page is the ordinary Roman printing licence and nothing more; the book is a bookseller's undertaking dedicated to the reigning pope, not a promulgation. Lesley says in his own preface why it was made: the Cisneros book had become so rare that it could not be had except for a great sum, and liturgical scholarship needed it in print again.
edition.publication: MISSALE MIXTUM SECUNDUM REGULAM BEATI ISIDORI DICTUM MOZARABES, PRAEFATIONE, NOTIS, ET APPENDICE AB ALEXANDRO LESLEO S. J. SACERDOTE ORNATUM. PARS PRIMA. ROMAE MDCCLV. Sumptibus Venantii Monaldini Bibliopolae in Via Cursus. TYPIS JOANNIS GENEROSI SALOMONI. SUPERIORUM PERMISSU. Dedicated by the bookseller Monaldini to Benedict XIV.
edition.title: Missale mixtum ... ab Alexandro Lesleo ornatum, Rome: Venantius Monaldini, 1755

work.author: Archdiocese of Toledo
work.description: The altar book of the Hispano-Mozarabic rite -- the old Spanish rite, the Visigothic and Isidorian use of the peninsula, suppressed for the Roman use in the eleventh century and kept alive at Toledo, where Cardinal Ximenez de Cisneros endowed the chapel of Corpus Christi in the cathedral for its celebration and had the Missale mixtum printed in 1500. IT IS NOT THE MISSALE ROMANUM AND MUST NOT BE FILED WITH IT: its Mass has its own shape, with the Illatio for the Preface, the Post pridie for what the Roman book puts after the institution narrative, the fraction of the Host into nine particles, and the Creed said after the consecration. It is registered under the archdiocese of Toledo because Toledo is the church whose ordinary has held and legislated for the rite continuously -- Cisneros for the 1500 printing, Lorenzana for the 1770s recension that Migne reprints -- on the same pattern as work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense. NEITHER EDITION REGISTERED HERE IS A TYPICAL EDITION AND NEITHER IS AN ACT. Both are scholarly reprintings of the Cisneros book: Alexander Lesley's of 1755, printed at Rome with his own preface, notes and appendix, and Migne's of 1862, which reprints Lesley in the Patrologia Latina. The rite's own modern book, the Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum promulgated at Toledo in 1991 and 1994, is in copyright, was not acquired, and has no record here.
work.title: Missale mixtum secundum regulam beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes
